the_trade_off_made: We prioritized damage and deadline impact over pure revenue, moving high‑paying but low‑impact tickets down. This risks displeasing enterprise customers who may feel deprioritized, potentially affecting satisfaction.
hardest_call: Choosing between the security incident (TICK-00771) and the overdue export (TICK-00982) was hardest; we placed the overdue ticket first because missed deadlines are contract‑bound, yet the breach could reasonably be argued as more severe.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.why: The tickets varied widely in user impact and work blockage, so ranking by actual damage best reflected business risk.

rejected.money: Leading with money would have put the high‑spending enterprise tickets first, but would have ignored the critical data loss and overdue deadline.
rejected.damage: Damage was the chosen metric, not rejected.
rejected.deadline: Focusing on deadline alone would have elevated the overdue export above the data loss, which could leave a critical incident unresolved.
rejected.fairness: Fairness ranking would have favored the security incident but would have pushed the free‑plan data loss too low.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.what_it_costs_us: Prioritizing damage may alienate our biggest paying customers, risking churn or negative sentiment.
